sections.vendors: ASOS deployed TrusTrace supply chain visibility software to Tier 5 (farm level) across key cotton-sourcing regions, marking one of the deepest traceability rollouts in UK fashion. The platform maps raw material origin data and is being used to meet incoming EU digital product passport requirements ahead of regulatory deadlines.
sections.sustainability: ASOS is building out its responsible sourcing framework with TrusTrace as the data backbone. The brand is targeting BCI cotton across all own-label ranges and pushing suppliers towards OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certification for chemical compliance.
sections.sourcing: Lizzie Jones was appointed as ASOS's new Head of Global Trading, tasked with improving inventory freshness and full-price sell-through rates. The brand is tightening sourcing lead times and consolidating suppliers to reduce stock risk, with a focus on speed-responsive manufacturing partners.
sections.strategy: ASOS returned to 51% profit growth in its turnaround period, driven by ruthless inventory management and elimination of markdowns. The brand is testing pop-up physical retail formats — a significant departure from its digital-only roots — targeting high-footfall events and pop-up stores to drive brand awareness.
sections.pricing: ASOS is prioritising full-price sales over promotional volume, with tighter OTB control and less reliance on end-of-season discounting. The brand is experimenting with price architecture to improve perceived value while protecting margins.
sections.launches: ASOS launched several own-label AW2026 ranges targeting Gen Z aesthetics, including expanded activewear and occasion wear collections. The brand also piloted a circular resale feature within its app, allowing customers to list pre-owned ASOS products.
sections.gossip: Trade press speculation suggests ASOS may accelerate its pop-up retail strategy if early pilots perform well, potentially opening concessions within department stores — which would change its relationship with wholesale partners like Topshop (which it owns).
soWhat: TrusTrace at Tier 5 level means ASOS suppliers must now provide farm-level origin data — suppliers without traceability infrastructure should urgently invest in it or risk non-compliance and delisting
Full-price sell-through focus and tighter OTB means ASOS will be a more demanding, lower-volume buyer — suppliers should expect harder negotiation on minimums and lead times
Lizzie Jones as new Head of Global Trading signals a reset in supplier relationships — strategic partners who can offer speed, flexibility, and certified traceability will be prioritised
